extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent prosecution staff who examine Hague (international design) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for USPTO examination of Hague (international) design applications, including identification, formal and substantive examination differences, figure/reproduction requirements, office communications, timing goals, and applicable statutes/regulations. Intended to instruct examiners how to process, object, refuse, and communicate regarding Hague cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize a Hague application
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to recognize an application as being a Hague (international design) application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hague cases are 35/ series cases in the U.S.: e.g., 35/5xx,xxx (Direct filing) and 35/0xx,xxx (Indirect filing). They appear as 'Special New' cases in PE2E and are time sensitive. Check PALM/DAV fields for International Registration Number, International Filing Date, International Registration Publication Date to confirm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish direct vs indirect filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between direct and indirect Hague applications and follow the correct filing/processing route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct filings go to the International Bureau (IB); indirect filings are received through an Office of Indirect Filing (OIF) which performs nominal review and transmits to IB. OIF checks entitlement to file through its office, may perform national security review, and may require a transmittal fee (USPTO as OIF conducts a national security review and requires a transmittal fee). See MPEP 2905.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand roles in the Hague process
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the responsibilities of the International Bureau (IB), Office of a Designated Contracting Party (CP), and Office of Indirect Filing (OIF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB examines formal requirements, registers designs, publishes in the International Design Bulletin, communicates registrations to designated CPs, transmits CP refusals to holders, processes renewals, and records changes. Office of a Designated CP conducts substantive examination under its national/regional law and may republish (USPTO issues a design patent to give effect). OIF performs nominal review (entitlement, security review, fees). See MPEP 2901 and 2905.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness goals for Hague examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Meet the timeliness goals for first office actions and understand the IB/CP refusal windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TC timeliness goal: 11 months to mail first action from the International Registration Publication Date. Under the Geneva Act, Offices have up to 12 months to refuse protection; USPTO's 12-month rule is codified at 37 CFR 1.1062(b) (a refusal may still be sent after 12 months if it was unintentionally not communicated). See MPEP 2901(II)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the effective filing (U.S.) date for a Hague application during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine effective filing date by considering the actual filing date and entitlement to priority to an earlier foreign or domestic filing. Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 384(a), the U.S. filing date for the Hague application is the international registration date. International registration date can be later than the international filing date in some cases. See MPEP 2906-2908.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements — IB examination vs CP refusal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the rule that the International Bureau examines formal requirements and that a Contracting Party cannot refuse effects of registration on form/content grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau examines whether applicable formal requirements under the Hague Agreement and Common Regulations have been satisfied (MPEP 2901(II)(B)). Article 12: A Contracting Party cannot refuse effects of international registration on grounds that requirements relating to the form or contents of the application have not been satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and handling of a Refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand what constitutes a Refusal of the effects of international registration and how to classify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Refusal is the first office action that refuses the effects of international registration (37 CFR 1.1062(b)). A Refusal may be a rejection, a restriction, or a Quayle. Note: a rejection following a restriction is NOT a Refusal. See MPEP 2901(II)(D) & 2920.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office communications and transmission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow proper transmission channels for office actions in Hague cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusals are transmitted from the USPTO solely to the IB, and the IB is responsible for forwarding the refusal to the applicant (regardless of POA). All other office actions are mailed directly to the applicant’s correspondence address or made available via Patent Center/PAIR for applicants opting for electronic notification. See MPEP 2920.05(a) and 2901(II)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions — definition and technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reproductions (photos, drawings, graphic representations) meet Hague technical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproductions refer to photographs, drawings, or other graphic representations illustrating the design. Relevant provisions include Hague Rule 9, Part Four of the Administrative Instructions, additional technical requirements for image files (WIPO link). See MPEP 2909.02 and 37 C.F.R. 1.1026 for U.S. requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Hague figure-numbering conventions when examining applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbers like 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 etc.; different embodiments start with the next consecutive number (2.1, 3.1, etc.). Sole figures listed as 1, 2, etc. (or 1.0, 2.0, etc. in older Hague cases). See MPEP 2920.05(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure descriptions — acceptable format
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not object to figure descriptions for not being formatted as independent/complete sentences; accept brief descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable formats include short notations like '1.1 : Front', '1.2 : Back', '1.3 : Left'. Hague Administrative Instructions Section 405 allows brief descriptions. The description should indicate the type of view (front, perspective, top, etc.) but is not required to be a complete sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure descriptions — requirement to include them
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure Hague applications include brief figure descriptions as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hague applications are required to have brief figure descriptions per Hague Rule 7(5)(a) and 37 CFR 1.1067. If missing, the specification can be objected to under 37 CFR 1.1067 and the examiner may suggest a specific form of descriptive text as an amendment (examples provided in slides). See MPEP 2920.04(a)(II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetitive figure descriptions are acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow figure descriptions that repeat the brief description or restate features; do not require their removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A feature description that also includes figure descriptions (repetitive of the brief description) should not be objected to. The examiner may suggest removal for clarity but cannot require removal of repetitive descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive language limits — impermissible content
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and act on descriptive language in specifications that is impermissible or functional rather than ornamental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive/specification language that describes functional uses or matters unrelated to the design may be objected to or rejected under 35 U.S.C. 171 or 35 U.S.C. 112 depending on how claims are worded. Example: language describing converting a shipping container into an aquarium with branding/illumination may be impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional language prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not permit statements in non-provisional international design applications that describe functional aspects or matter unrelated to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification is not permitted to include statements describing matters that are directed to function or are unrelated to the design. Use form paragraphs 15.41 and/or 15.46.01 (MPEP 1503.01(II)) where appropriate. See MPEP 2920.04(a)(II).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to figure descriptions — formal vs substantive
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between formal objections (which should not be required) and substantive objections (which may be required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections to purely formal matters should not be given as requirements; examiners may request/suggest corrections without making them mandatory. However, substantive objections (e.g., 'transparent' vs 'translucent' having different appearances) are appropriate and the examiner may require amendment for clarity of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing reproduction mediums — consistency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not permit mixing different reproduction media or mixing black & white and color within the same design embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No mixing of reproductions using different mediums in the same design (embodiment); no mixing of black & white and color in the same design/embodiment. Such mixing in the same design may justify objection, 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection, or other action; acceptable if in separate designs (restriction may still be appropriate). See MPEP 1503.02(V).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing deficiencies handling (37 CFR 1.84/1.152)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that drawing deficiencies are handled differently for Hague applications compared to U.S. design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawing deficiencies should not be objected to under 37 CFR 1.84 or 1.152 for Hague applications. Follow Hague-specific drawing/reproduction rules (see MPEP 2920.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Certificate of Priority Application (CPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file a CPA in Hague international design applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.53(d)(ii): CPA cannot be filed in Hague International Design Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 37 CFR 1.312 amendments permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow properly filed 37 CFR 1.312 amendments in Hague applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly filed 312 amendments may be used in Hague applications (slide note: 'Properly filed 312 amendments may be used in Hague applications').

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee payment process for Hague cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Hague-specific issue fee payment options and compute the correct fee amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may pay the issue fee to the USPTO (in dollars) or through the IB (in Swiss francs). If paid through IB, IB notifies USPTO and an IFEE document appears in the file. The issue fee amount due is the amount in effect as of the international registration date, so fees may differ from contemporaneous 29/ series applications. See MPEP 2920.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination under national law remains applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply substantive examination requirements of the designated Contracting Party's national/regional law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of a Designated CP conducts substantive examination to the extent required under its national/regional law. Some CPs republish (e.g., USPTO issues a design patent giving effect to design rights). Substantive examination procedures and enforcement remain the same as national practice. See MPEP 2901(II)(D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and use of relevant authorities and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the listed statutes, regulations, MPEP sections, Hague Agreement instruments, and WIPO resources to guide examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key authorities: 35 U.S.C. §§ 381–390; 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.1001–1.1071; MPEP 2900 and 1500; Hague Agreement Articles, Regulations, Administrative Instructions; WIPO technical requirements for reproductions. Use Patent Center and WIPO Hague/Design databases for searches and file wrapper information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching Hague registrations and file wrappers
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate Hague registrations and associated file wrapper/office actions for examination and public searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Patent Center (https://patentcenter.uspto.gov/) for U.S. file wrapper and office actions. Search Hague registrations at WIPO Hague Express and Global Design Database (links provided in slides). Consult Hague Administrative Instructions, Rules, and Common Regulations on WIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIF nominal review duties
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO acts as an Office of Indirect Filing, perform only the permitted nominal review tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIF should check that the applicant is entitled to file through its office, may conduct a national security review, and may require a transmittal fee; OIFs generally do not conduct substantive examination. See MPEP 2905 and 37 CFR 1.9(n).
